source.title: Long SKILL Compliance as Logical Reasoning: Closure-Grounded Detection with Scaling-Guided On-Policy Distillation
source.authors: Shuai Zhao; Feng-Mei Ni; Li-Chao Ma; Jia-Ye Lin; Fei Han; Yang Wei; Lu Pan

record.file_problem: The text includes the main paper and conclusion, but ends abruptly during Appendix D.3. It is not abstract-only.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures and models downstream compliance-detection correctness against model scale, a different measure and task from the original pretraining-loss scaling studies.
record.gate_note: The study fits a task-specific relationship between Qwen3.5 model scale, policy-graph complexity, and end-to-end correctness, and reports a 27B validation result. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss, training tokens or compute, compute-optimal allocation, or architecture-shape effects. The method-comparison and OPD results do not independently test the claim versions about pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: The study fits end-to-end compliance-detection correctness against parameter count for four Qwen3.5 checkpoints (0.8B to 9B) and checks a held-out 27B checkpoint. That is a downstream-predictability result (V6) in a new task setting. It does not measure pretraining loss, tokens, compute, allocation or shape. The fit is a saturating logistic, not a power law.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that model scale and CDG-derived policy complexity jointly predict compliance-detection correctness. They describe the relationship as saturating with scale, with complexity acting as residual instance difficulty (the selected form has no scale-complexity interaction). They use it to choose models and prioritise OPD samples. Their 27B validation is stated only qualitatively.
record.recipe_differences: This is a task-specific fit of downstream compliance correctness against model scale and policy complexity, not a held-out cross-entropy loss scaling experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted correctness trend varies with policy-graph complexity: low-complexity samples converge rapidly, while high-complexity samples are harder and show larger gains from increasing scale. The study also fits across five datasets, but the text's detailed trend description is for the three business datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Instance-level policy-graph complexity predicts residual difficulty across checkpoints. The selected form has no scale-by-complexity interaction, yet high-complexity samples show larger probability gains from scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-instance structural complexity modulates how much downstream accuracy improves with model scale.

record.problems: The scaling analysis uses Qwen3.5 checkpoints and compliance correctness rather than pretraining loss. Figure 3's numerical values are not given in the text; the stated 27B validation is qualitative. The text ends during Appendix D.3.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-related rows retained. Table 2 compares policy-access methods and model families for detection effectiveness, but those method comparisons are not the fitted scale-and-complexity result; OPD results measure the training strategy rather than the scaling relationship itself.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No loss extrapolation. Only a qualitative downstream-correctness extrapolation to 27B, recorded under V6.
No architecture-shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or training regimes are scaled.
Prediction from pretraining loss is not tested. Scale prediction is tested only in one model family and one task type.
Model selection among task-specific logistic forms only. Nothing on pretraining-law exponents or allocation.

missing.what: Per-checkpoint ACC/F1 for Qwen3.5-4B, 9B and 27B under RawSkill, LightRAG and SkillCDG, showing non-monotonic scaling (e.g. SkillCDG Fulfillment ACC 54.4/50.0/67.6; F1 54.3/50.0/46.5)
Leave-one-scale-out prediction error and the numerical 27B predicted-vs-observed comparison; the text describes both but reports no values
Model comparison (Eq. 3 vs additive vs nested saturating with lambda=0) and fitted parameter values; the text says the data favour the no-interaction saturating form
4B base vs 9B teacher F1 under SkillCDG representation (50.3 vs 55.0 Fulfillment; 52.6 vs 53.8 AfterSales; 52.9 vs 58.0 MerchantSupport). These differ from the Table 2 4B/9B values.

record.verdict_notes: Downstream-only, single-family (Qwen3.5) study. The functional form is a saturating logistic in N, not a power law. All RQ2 evidence is figure-only or qualitative. The text's own Table 2 shows several cases where larger Qwen3.5 checkpoints score lower, which the RQ2 narrative does not discuss. Table 6 4B and 9B numbers are inconsistent with Table 2. Text truncated in Appendix D.3.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of loss on much larger runs from small-run loss fits.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Scaling-law form in other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests predictability for compliance-detection correctness, not general downstream tasks or performance as a function of pretraining loss.
Dependence of original scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting choices, and whether original loss curves bend away from power laws.

relationships.condition: Fitted scale-complexity correctness model, Qwen3.5 0.8B-9B on the business datasets, with qualitative 27B check
relationships.reason: Authors report correctness rising and saturating with scale, larger gains on high-complexity samples, and 27B matching the fit. All qualitative, figure-only (r1-r7).
relationships.display_finding: Correctness increased toward saturation, with larger gains on high-complexity samples and qualitative agreement between the 27B model and the fitted curve.

relationships.condition: Raw per-checkpoint results in Table 2 (Qwen3.5 4B/9B/27B, RawSkill and SkillCDG, ACC and F1)
relationships.reason: Based on the text, not rows: improvement with scale is non-monotonic. For SkillCDG, 9B is below 4B on Fulfillment (ACC 50.0 vs 54.4) and MerchantSupport (50.8 vs 56.0). 27B F1 is below 4B on AfterSales (40.7 vs 50.6). Predictability depends on metric and setting.
relationships.display_finding: SkillCDG 9B underperformed 4B on Fulfillment accuracy (50.0 versus 54.4) and MerchantSupport accuracy (50.8 versus 56.0), while 27B underperformed 4B on AfterSales F1 (40.7 versus 50.6).
